sanskrit: tapyamānaṃ tathā rāmaṃ sītāharaṇakarśitam lokānām abhave yuktaṃ sāmvartakam ivānalam
english: Rāma, tormented and emaciated by Sītā's abduction, blazed like the doomsday fire fit for the destruction of all worlds.

sanskrit: vīkṣamāṇaṃ dhanuḥ sajyaṃ niḥśvasantaṃ muhur muhuḥ hantukāmaṃ paśuṃ rudraṃ kruddhaṃ dakṣakratau yathā
english: He gazed upon his strung bow and breathed repeatedly in fury, like Rudra enraged and desiring to slay the sacrificial beast at Dakṣa's sacrifice.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ saṃkruddhaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ mukhena pariśuṣyatā
english: Seeing Rāma enraged as never before, Lakṣmaṇa spoke words with folded hands and a parched mouth.

sanskrit: purā bhūtvā mṛdur dāntaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ na krodhavaśam āpannaḥ prakṛtiṃ hātum arhasi
english: "You who were formerly gentle, self-restrained, and devoted to the welfare of all beings — you should not abandon your nature by falling under the sway of anger.

sanskrit: candre lakṣṇīḥ prabhā sūrye gatir vāyau bhuvi kṣamā etac ca niyataṃ sarvaṃ tvayi cānuttamaṃ yaśaḥ
english: Splendour belongs to the moon, radiance to the sun, speed to the wind, patience to the earth — all these are fixed qualities — and in you, unsurpassed glory.

sanskrit: na tu jānāmi kasyāyaṃ bhagnaḥ sāṃgrāmiko rathaḥ kena vā kasya vā hetoḥ sāyudhaḥ saparicchadaḥ
english: I do not know to whom this shattered war-chariot belongs, armed and fully equipped as it is, nor by whom or for what reason it was destroyed.

sanskrit: khuranemikṣataś cāyaṃ sikto rudhirabindubhiḥ deśo nivṛttasaṃgrāmaḥ sughoraḥ pārthivātmaja
english: This place is scarred by hooves and wheel-rims, sprinkled with drops of blood — a very dreadful spot where battle was joined and then ended, O son of a king.

sanskrit: ekasya tu vimardo 'yaṃ na dvayor vadatāṃ vara na hi vṛttaṃ hi paśyāmi balasya mahataḥ padam
english: The marks of combat here are those of a single fighter, not two — I see no trace, O best of speakers, of a large army having passed this way.

sanskrit: naikasya tu kṛte lokān vināśayitum arhasi yuktadaṇḍā hi mṛdavaḥ praśāntā vasudhādhipāḥ
english: You should not destroy the worlds on account of a single person. Lords of the earth who are gentle and tranquil apply punishment in due measure.

sanskrit: sadā tvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ śaraṇyaḥ paramā gatiḥ ko nu dārapraṇāśaṃ te sādhu manyeta rāghava
english: You are ever the refuge and supreme resort of all beings, O Rāghava — who then would consider it good that you should lose your wife?

sanskrit: saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailā devagandharvadānavāḥ nālaṃ te vipriyaṃ kartuṃ dīkṣitasyeva sādhavaḥ
english: Rivers, oceans, mountains, gods, gandharvas, and dānavas are not capable of doing what is displeasing to you, as the virtuous are not capable of wronging one who has taken a sacred vow.

sanskrit: yena rājan hṛtā sītā tam anveṣitum arhasi maddvitīyo dhanuṣpāṇiḥ sahāyaiḥ paramarṣibhiḥ
english: O king, you should seek out the one by whom Sītā was abducted — with me at your side, bow in hand, and with the great sages as allies.

sanskrit: samudraṃ ca viceṣyāmaḥ parvatāṃś ca vanāni ca guhāś ca vividhā ghorā nalinīḥ pārvatīś ca ha
english: We shall search the ocean, the mountains, the forests, the many dreadful caves, the lotus-ponds, and the highland lakes.

sanskrit: devagandharvalokāṃś ca viceṣyāmaḥ samāhitāḥ yāvan nādhigamiṣyāmas tava bhāryāpahāriṇam
english: We shall search the worlds of gods and gandharvas as well, with concentrated minds, until we find the abductor of your wife.

sanskrit: na cet sāmnā pradāsyanti patnīṃ te tridaśeśvarāḥ kosalendra tataḥ paścāt prāptakālaṃ kariṣyasi
english: If even the lords of the thirty gods do not return your wife through conciliation, O lord of Kosala, you will then act as the occasion demands.

sanskrit: śīlena sāmnā vinayena sītāṃ nayena na prāpsyasi cen narendra tataḥ samutsādaya hemapuṅkhair mahendravajrapratimaiḥ śaraughaiḥ
english: If through good conduct, conciliation, humility, and policy you cannot recover Sītā, O lord of men, then annihilate them with showers of arrows gold-feathered and equal to Mahendra's thunderbolt."

sanskrit: taṃ tathā śokasaṃtaptaṃ vilapantam anāthavat mohena mahatāviṣṭaṃ paridyūnam acetanam
english: Rāma was thus tormented by grief, lamenting like one without a protector, seized by great delusion, utterly dispirited and bereft of consciousness.

sanskrit: tataḥ saumitrir āśvāsya muhūrtād iva lakṣmaṇaḥ rāmaṃ saṃbodhayām āsa caraṇau cābhipīḍayan
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, after consoling him for what seemed like a moment, began to rouse Rāma, pressing his feet.

sanskrit: mahatā tapasā rāma mahatā cāpi karmaṇā rājñā daśarathenāsīl labdho 'mṛtam ivāmaraiḥ
english: "You were obtained, O Rāma, by king Daśaratha through great austerity and great deeds, as the immortals obtained amṛta.

sanskrit: tava caiva guṇair baddhas tvadviyogān mahīpatiḥ rājā devatvam āpanno bharatasya yathā śrutam
english: Bound by your qualities and unable to bear separation from you, that lord of the earth, the king, has attained divine status — so it is heard from Bharata.

sanskrit: yadi duḥkham idaṃ prāptaṃ kākutstha na sahiṣyase prākṛtaś cālpasattvaś ca itaraḥ kaḥ sahiṣyati
english: If you, O Kākutstha, cannot endure this grief that has befallen you, what other ordinary man of little strength shall endure it?

sanskrit: duḥkhito hi bhavāṃl lokāṃs tejasā yadi dhakṣyate ārtāḥ prajā naravyāghra kva nu yāsyanti nirvṛtim
english: If in your distress you were to scorch the worlds with your energy, O tiger among men, where would the afflicted subjects go to find peace?

sanskrit: lokasvabhāva evaiṣa yayātir nahuṣātmajaḥ gataḥ śakreṇa sālokyam anayas taṃ samaspṛśat
english: This is the very nature of the world: Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, had attained the same realm as Śakra, and yet calamity touched him as well.

sanskrit: maharṣayo vasiṣṭhas tu yaḥ pitur naḥ purohitaḥ ahnā putraśataṃ jajñe tathaivāsya punar hatam
english: The great seer Vasiṣṭha, who was the household priest of our father, begat a hundred sons in a single day — and those same sons were slain.

sanskrit: yā ceyaṃ jagato mātā devī lokanamaskṛtā asyāś ca calanaṃ bhūmer dṛśyate satyasaṃśrava
english: And the goddess who is the mother of the world and revered by all — even the trembling of the earth, her quaking, is seen, O you to whom truth is a vow.

sanskrit: yau cemau jagatāṃ netre yatra sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam ādityacandrau grahaṇam abhyupetau mahābalau
english: And these two eyes of the world, the sun and moon — in whom all things are established — even they, mighty as they are, are seized by eclipses.

sanskrit: sumahānty api bhūtāni devāś ca puruṣarṣabha na daivasya pramuñcanti sarvabhūtāni dehinaḥ
english: Even the mightiest beings and the gods, O bull among men — no embodied creature in all existence is released from the power of fate.

sanskrit: śakrādiṣv api deveṣu vartamānau nayānayau śrūyete naraśārdūla na tvaṃ vyathitum arhasi
english: Even among the gods headed by Śakra, both good fortune and misfortune are heard to occur, O tiger among men — you should not be distressed.

sanskrit: naṣṭāyām api vaidehyāṃ hṛtāyām api cānagha śocituṃ nārhase vīra yathānyaḥ prākṛtas tathā
english: Even though Vaidehī is lost, even though she has been abducted, O sinless one, you should not grieve as another ordinary man would, O hero.

sanskrit: tvadvidhā hi na śocanti satataṃ satyadarśinaḥ sumahatsv api kṛcchreṣu rāmānirviṇṇadarśaṇāḥ
english: Those like you who constantly behold truth and who, like Rāma, are never despondent, do not grieve even in the greatest of adversities.

sanskrit: tattvato hi naraśreṣṭha buddhyā samanucintaya buddhyā yuktā mahāprājñā vijānanti śubhāśubhe
english: Reflect carefully upon reality with your intellect, O best of men. The greatly wise, endowed with discernment, know the auspicious from the inauspicious.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭaguṇadoṣāṇām adhṛtānāṃ ca karmaṇām nāntareṇa kriyāṃ teṣāṃ phalam iṣṭaṃ pravartate
english: For actions whose merits and faults are unseen and which are not firmly undertaken, the desired fruit does not come to pass without effort.

sanskrit: mām eva hi purā vīra tvam eva bahuṣo 'nvaśāḥ anuśiṣyād dhi ko nu tvām api sākṣād bṛhaspatiḥ
english: O hero, it was you yourself who instructed me repeatedly in the past. Who indeed could teach you now — even Bṛhaspati himself in person?

sanskrit: buddhiś ca te mahāprājña devair api duranvayā śokenābhiprasuptaṃ te jñānaṃ saṃbodhayāmy aham
english: Your wisdom, O greatly wise one, is unsurpassed even by the gods. I am awakening your knowledge that has fallen asleep under grief.

sanskrit: divyaṃ ca mānuṣaṃ caivam ātmanaś ca parākramam ikṣvākuvṛṣabhāvekṣya yatasva dviṣatāṃ badhe
english: Considering your own divine and human prowess, O bull of the Ikṣvāku line, strive for the destruction of your enemies.

sanskrit: kiṃ te sarvavināśena kṛtena puruṣarṣabha tam eva tu ripuṃ pāpaṃ vijñāyoddhartum arhasi
english: What is the use of destroying everything, O bull among men? You should identify that one wicked enemy and root him out."

sanskrit: pūrvajo 'py uktamātras tu lakṣmaṇena subhāṣitam sāragrāhī mahāsāraṃ pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ
english: Though Rāma was the elder, upon hearing Lakṣmaṇa's excellent speech, Rāghava, being one who grasps the essence, accepted the great substance of what was said.

sanskrit: saṃnigṛhya mahābāhuḥ pravṛddhaṃ kopam ātmanaḥ avaṣṭabhya dhanuś citraṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: The mighty-armed Rāma, suppressing his swollen anger and firmly gripping his splendid bow, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: kiṃ kariṣyāvahe vatsa kva vā gacchāva lakṣmaṇa kenopāyena paśyeyaṃ sītām iti vicintaya
english: "What shall we do, dear one? Where shall we go, Lakṣmaṇa? By what means might I see Sītā? Think on this."

sanskrit: taṃ tathā paritāpārtaṃ lakṣmaṇo rāmam abravīt idam eva janasthānaṃ tvam anveṣitum arhasi
english: Lakṣmaṇa spoke to Rāma, who was thus afflicted with burning anguish: "This very Janasthāna you should search."

sanskrit: rākṣasair bahubhiḥ kīrṇaṃ nānādrumalatāyutam santīha giridurgāṇi nirdarāḥ kandarāṇi ca
english: "Swarming with many rākṣasas and filled with diverse trees and creepers, there are here mountain fastnesses, cliffs, and ravines,

sanskrit: guhāś ca vividhā ghorā nānāmṛgagaṇākulāḥ āvāsāḥ kiṃnarāṇāṃ ca gandharvabhavanāni ca
english: And many dreadful caves teeming with various herds of animals, the abodes of kiṃnaras, and the dwelling-places of gandharvas.

sanskrit: tāni yukto mayā sārdhaṃ tvam anveṣitum arhasi tvadvidho buddhisaṃpannā māhātmāno nararṣabha
english: Those places you, accompanied by me, should search. Great-souled ones endowed with intellect such as yours, O bull among men,

sanskrit: āpatsu na prakampante vāyuvegair ivācalāḥ ity uktas tad vanaṃ sarvaṃ vicacāra salakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Are not shaken in adversities, like mountains in the gusts of the wind." So addressed, Rāma ranged through that entire forest together with Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: kruddho rāmaḥ śaraṃ ghoraṃ saṃdhāya dhanuṣi kṣuram tataḥ parvatakūṭābhaṃ mahābhāgaṃ dvijottamam
english: Rāma, enraged, fitting a dreadful razor-headed arrow to his bow, then saw the most noble bird, that foremost among twice-born creatures, like a mountain peak,

sanskrit: dadarśa patitaṃ bhūmau kṣatajārdraṃ jaṭāyuṣam taṃ dṛṣṭvā giriśṛṅgābhaṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt anena sītā vaidehī bhakṣitā nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Jaṭāyu, lying fallen on the ground, drenched in blood. Seeing him who resembled a mountain summit, Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa: "Sītā Vaidehī has been devoured by this one — there is no doubt."

sanskrit: gṛdhrarūpam idaṃ vyaktaṃ rakṣo bhramati kānanam bhakṣayitvā viśālākṣīm āste sītāṃ yathāsukham enaṃ vadhiṣye dīptāgrair ghorair bāṇair ajihmagaiḥ
english: "Clearly this rākṣasa in the form of a vulture wanders the forest; having devoured Sītā of the wide eyes, it rests at ease. I shall slay it with my blazing-tipped, dreadful, straight-flying arrows."

sanskrit: ity uktvābhyapatad gṛdhraṃ saṃdhāya dhanuṣi kṣuram kruddho rāmaḥ samudrāntāṃ cālayann iva medinīm
english: Having spoken thus, the enraged Rāma rushed toward the vulture, fitting the razor-headed arrow to his bow, as if shaking the earth to its ocean-bounded ends.

sanskrit: taṃ dīnadīnayā vācā saphenaṃ rudhiraṃ vaman abhyabhāṣata pakṣī tu rāmaṃ daśarathātmajam
english: But the bird, vomiting frothy blood, addressed Rāma, son of Daśaratha, in a voice pitifully feeble:

sanskrit: yām oṣadhim ivāyuṣmann anveṣasi mahāvane sā devī mama ca prāṇā rāvaṇenobhayaṃ hṛtam
english: "That goddess whom you seek in the great forest, O long-lived one, like a healing herb — she and my very life-breath have both been carried off by Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tvayā virahitā devī lakṣmaṇena ca rāghava hriyamāṇā mayā dṛṣṭā rāvaṇena balīyasā
english: The goddess separated from you and Lakṣmaṇa, O Rāghava, being carried away by the mighty Rāvaṇa — she was seen by me.

sanskrit: sītām abhyavapan no 'haṃ rāvaṇaś ca raṇe mayā vidhvaṃsitarathacchatraḥ pātito dharaṇītale
english: I fell upon Sītā's abductor and upon Rāvaṇa in battle; by me his chariot and parasol were shattered and he was brought down to the ground.

sanskrit: etad asya dhanur bhagnam etad asya śarāvaram ayam asya raṇe rāma bhagnaḥ sāṃgrāmiko rathaḥ
english: This is his shattered bow, this is his quiver of arrows, and this, O Rāma, is his war-chariot broken in battle.

sanskrit: pariśrāntasya me pakṣau chittvā khaḍgena rāvaṇaḥ sītām ādāya vaidehīm utpapāta vihāyasaṃ rakṣasā nihataṃ pūrvma na māṃ hantuṃ tvam arhasi
english: When I was exhausted, Rāvaṇa cut off my wings with his sword; having seized Sītā Vaidehī, he soared into the sky. I was struck down first by the rākṣasa — you should not slay me."

sanskrit: rāmas tasya tu vijñāya sītāsaktāṃ priyāṃ kathām gṛdhrarājaṃ pariṣvajya ruroda sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Rāma, understanding that the beloved tale was bound up with Sītā, embraced the king of vultures and wept together with Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: ekam ekāyane durge niḥśvasantaṃ kathaṃ cana samīkṣya duḥkhito rāmaḥ saumitrim idam abravīt
english: Seeing the solitary one lying alone on that impassable ground, barely breathing, grief-stricken Rāma spoke these words to the son of Sumitrā:

sanskrit: rājyād bhraṃśo vane vāsaḥ sītā naṣṭā hato dvijaḥ īdṛśīyaṃ mamālakṣmīr nirdahed api pāvakam
english: "Expulsion from the kingdom, dwelling in the forest, Sītā lost, and now a twice-born creature slain — such is my misfortune; it would burn even fire.

sanskrit: saṃpūrṇam api ced adya pratareyaṃ mahodadhim so 'pi nūnaṃ mamālakṣmyā viśuṣyet saritāṃ patiḥ
english: Were I even today to cross the full expanse of the great ocean, the lord of rivers would surely dry up from my ill-luck.

sanskrit: nāsty abhāgyataro loke matto 'smin sacarācare yeneyaṃ mahatī prāptā mayā vyasanavāgurā
english: There is none more unfortunate than I in this world of moving and unmoving things, for this great snare of calamity has ensnared me.

sanskrit: ayaṃ pitṛvayasyo me gṛdhrarājo jarānvitaḥ śete vinihato bhūmau mama bhāgyaviparyayāt
english: This king of vultures, who was like a father to me, aged and venerable, lies slain on the ground by reason of my misfortune."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā bahuśo rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ jaṭāyuṣaṃ ca pasparśa pitṛsnehaṃ nidarśayan
english: Having spoken thus many times, Rāghava, together with Lakṣmaṇa, touched Jaṭāyu, showing the affection of a father.

sanskrit: nikṛttapakṣaṃ rudhirāvasiktaṃ taṃ gṛdhrarājaṃ parirabhya rāmaḥ kva maithili prāṇasamā mameti vimucya vācaṃ nipapāta bhūmau
english: Embracing that king of vultures whose wings had been cut off and who was drenched in blood, Rāma released from his lips the words — "Where are you, O Maithilī, you who are equal to my very life?" — and fell to the ground.
